originalPreBoundary:
My adult sister had a spare key to my apartment while I worked nights. We had agreed she would ask before coming over.

At home I found her coat and school bag on the chair. She had come in with the key without asking and then gone back into the building hallway. She took evening classes.

My own phone was in my hand. Her message said, “I’m in the hallway. Please don’t tell Mum I’m here.”

She had told me earlier that she had argued with Mum, but not why.

I went into the building hallway. My sister stood outside my apartment door. She said, “Can I stay tonight?”

I had promised my partner that we would have the flat to ourselves before an early medical appointment. My partner was not home yet. I did not know whether my sister had anywhere else safe to go.

My sister said she could wait there while I went back into the flat to think. I went back inside. I could return to her without making her leave. Her coat and bag remained on the chair, and I kept my phone.

I could invite her in now, ask what had happened before agreeing, or say tonight could not work and offer to help find somewhere. I did not know what answer I would get or whether another place could be found.

I wanted her to have somewhere safe. I also wanted to keep my promise and our agreement about the key. I hadn’t agreed to a stay yet.

revealSource.text:
I told my sister I would let her stay, but that I would tell my partner before bringing her back in. I then told my partner before inviting her inside.

I couldn’t promise my partner a private evening and secretly give it away. I also couldn’t ask my sister to leave without knowing where she would go.

Later that night, my sister told me she had missed the last bus. The argument with Mum was still not explained. I had let her stay that night; we did not settle a new rule about the key.
